advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard build_surface()'s getattr on __all__ entries so a missing/lazy name is reported as drift (or a clear error) rather than an uncaught AttributeError.
evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:155-156: `for name in public_names(module): members[name] = _describe(getattr(module, name))`
ABSENCE: no try/except or membership check around getattr, and no test exercises an __all__ entry that is not a live attribute
advisory.finding: On the __all__ path, build_surface() calls getattr(module, name) for every name in module.__all__ with no guard; if __all__ lists a name that is lazily provided (via module __getattr__) or is stale/misspelled, getattr raises AttributeError and aborts --check with an uncaught traceback instead of emitting a clean drift report and the --update remediation hint.
scenarios: A module exports a name via __all__ that is resolved lazily through module-level __getattr__ or that becomes stale after a rename
Author runs the gate expecting a drift report but instead gets an AttributeError traceback

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the module-less-constant branch of _owns so imported constant re-exports are not counted as owned by a pinned module (or document that module-less constants are always pinned regardless of true origin).
evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:70-72: `owner = getattr(obj, "__module__", None)` then `if owner is None: return True`
scripts/gen_api_surface.py:26 (docstring): '— excluding imported re-exports and submodules.'

Modules contracts/findings/prompts/runner use the owned path (only rebar, rebar.signing, rebar.llm.workflow.executor define __all__ per the docstring), so their constant re-exports flow through this branch
advisory.finding: _owns() returns True for any object whose __module__ is None, which for the owned-attribute path (contracts/findings/prompts/runner — modules without __all__) means an imported constant re-export (any module-less instance such as a tuple/frozenset/int/str imported `from other import X`) is captured as if the module owns it, contradicting the docstring's 'excluding imported re-exports' guarantee.
scenarios: A pinned module does `from constants import SEVERITIES` and re-exports it; the gate attributes SEVERITIES to the pinned module even though it is a re-export
A shared constant is renamed/moved in its true owning module but a stale re-export keeps it visible under a pinned module

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether inherited public methods are part of the guarded class shape; if not, restrict _describe_class to methods defined on the class itself.
evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:119: `for name, member in inspect.getmembers(obj, callable):`
scripts/gen_api_surface.py:120-124: only leading-underscore names (except __init__) are skipped; inherited public methods are retained
advisory.finding: _describe_class() uses inspect.getmembers(obj, callable) which also enumerates inherited public methods from base classes that may live in unpinned modules; a signature change in such a base class will trip the drift gate for a pinned subclass and the class descriptor mixes owned and inherited shape.
scenarios: A pinned class subclasses a base defined in a module not listed in MODULES; changing that base's public method signature surfaces as CHANGED on the subclass

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add RED→GREEN tests injecting a class-shape drift (e.g. remove a RunRequest field) and a constant-value drift and asserting gen.main(['--check']) == 1 with the expected CHANGED line.
evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:8: "changed class shape (bases, dataclass fields, public-method signatures), or a changed public constant"
scripts/gen_api_surface.py:100 _describe_class computes bases/fields/methods; scripts/gen_api_surface.py:140 _value_repr computes pinned constant values — both added lines

Only test_check_trips_when_a_signature_changes injects CHANGED drift, and it mutates a callable param name (params[0][0] = 'renamed_first_arg'); no test mutates a class descriptor (e.g. surface['rebar.llm.runner']['RunRequest']['fields'].remove('config')) or a constant (e.g. surface['rebar.llm.prompting.prompts']['PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION']['value']) and asserts gen.main(['--check']) == 1
advisory.finding: The gate's contract explicitly covers 'a changed class shape' and 'a changed public constant' (docstring lines 8-9), and the descriptor builders _describe_class (bases/dataclass fields/method signatures) and _value_repr (constant values) are all newly-added lines, but no RED→GREEN test injects a class-shape drift or a constant-value drift and asserts --check fails. The CHANGED code path is exercised only by a single parameter-rename test (test_check_trips_when_a_signature_changes). A regression that stopped capturing dataclass fields, class bases, or constant values in the descriptor would not be caught by any drift-detection test.
scenarios: A refactor that drops __dataclass_fields__ capture, or stops pinning constant values, would leave the gate green despite a public-surface regression it claims to guard.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two tests mirroring test_check_trips_when_a_signature_changes: one popping/altering surface['rebar.llm.runner']['RunRequest']['fields'] and one altering surface['rebar.llm.prompting.prompts']['PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION']['value'], each asserting gen.main(['--check']) == 1 and the matching '~ CHANGED' line.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace pytest.importorskip('yaml') with a hard import (or remove the guard) since pyyaml is a required core dependency, so the workflow-executor subsumption assertion always runs.
evidence: pyproject.toml:63: "pyyaml>=6" (a required core dependency, per pyproject.toml:46-47 'loading + running a `.rebar/workflows/*.yaml` workflow cannot have an optional parser')
advisory.finding: test_subsumes_workflow_executor_surface guards its assertions behind pytest.importorskip('yaml'), but pyyaml is a REQUIRED core dependency (pyproject.toml lists 'pyyaml>=6' as non-optional), so an environment missing yaml is a real regression the skip would mask rather than a legitimately-optional path. The subsumption coverage this test provides for run_workflow silently vanishes if the required dependency ever fails to install.
scenarios: If pyyaml is absent from the environment, this subsumption test skips silently instead of failing, hiding both the missing dependency and any loss of run_workflow surface coverage.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the importorskip and import yaml unconditionally (or rely on run_workflow being in the surface), so a missing required dependency fails the test rather than skipping it.
